[Guide index](start-here.html) | Guide 2 of 5

These remote snippets are not executed during package builds. Start a THIP R
session using the [setup guide](start-here.html), then connect:

```{r connect, eval=FALSE}
library(thipR)
library(dplyr)
con <- thip_connect()
```

## Prepare compatible tables and dates

```{r table, eval=FALSE}
ipd <- thip_table(
  con, tables = c("nhso2567", "nhso2568"), .id = "source_table",
  dates = c(adm = "dateadm", dsc = "datedsc", death = "death_date"),
  date_format = c(adm = "%Y%m%d", dsc = "%Y%m%d", death = "%Y-%m-%d")
)
```

This stacks compatible schemas using `UNION ALL`; it does not deduplicate,
resolve identifiers or harmonize clinical meaning. Use distributed names, not
`_local` tables. Keep incompatible sources, such as vaccinations and admissions,
separate. `thip_columns()` uses singular `table` because it describes one table;
`thip_table()` uses plural `tables` because it may combine several.

Temporal mappings preserve original columns and add new ones. Formats are
explicit: `%Y%m%d`, `%Y-%m-%d`, `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S`, or
`%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS` (optional one to three fractional digits). You may supply one
format per mapping group or a named format vector keyed by output name. This is
a supported subset of R-style formats, not arbitrary `strptime()` syntax.
Malformed/impossible dates and dates outside 1900–2299 become `NA`. Date output
uses the source calendar date; requesting a date from timestamp text discards
its time. Inspect original values when assessing missing or invalid dates.

### Audit conversion explicitly

Different columns can use different formats. The example above configures compact
admission/discharge text and ISO death-date text; confirm the source contract for
your selected tables. A single format applied to every field can turn nonblank
death dates into missing values. Keep the raw columns until after the audit.

```{r date-audit-db, eval=FALSE}
# This executes aggregate SELECT queries; only the summary enters R.
# Choose the source tables/scope deliberately: this can scan each selected field.
date_quality <- thip_date_audit(
  ipd,
  columns = c(adm = "dateadm", dsc = "datedsc", death = "death_date"),
  by = "source_table"
)
```

Do this before filtering on `adm` or `death`: filtering out missing converted
dates would conceal failures. The helper compares existing raw/converted pairs;
it does not guess formats or repair values. Missing source text (`n_missing`),
whitespace/empty strings (`n_blank`), successful nonblank conversions (`n_parsed`)
and unsuccessful nonblank conversions (`n_failed`) are separate. A nonzero
`n_inconsistent` means a missing/blank source has a nonmissing converted value.
Successful parsing does not establish death ascertainment or clinical plausibility.

Here is a runnable, entirely synthetic illustration of those categories. The
converted column represents the strict conversion result, including an impossible
date becoming missing.

```{r date-audit-synthetic}
example_dates <- data.frame(
  raw = c("20240229", "20230229", "", "   ", NA_character_),
  day = as.Date(c("2024-02-29", NA, NA, NA, NA))
)
thipR::thip_date_audit(example_dates, columns = c(day = "raw"))
```

For a COVID-style timestamp source, choose date-only or datetime deliberately:

```{r datetime, eval=FALSE}
vaccination_days <- thip_table(
  con, tables = "covid2023",
  dates = c(vaccination_day = "immunization_date"),
  date_format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS"
)

# Set source_timezone only after the data provider confirms its meaning.
# It must be an IANA zone name; do not infer it from your computer or locale.
vaccination_times <- thip_table(
  con, tables = "covid2023",
  datetimes = c(vaccinated_at = "immunization_date"),
  datetime_format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
  timezone = source_timezone
)
```

Datetime output preserves milliseconds. Offset-bearing text is not supported;
ambiguous daylight-saving times require upstream resolution. `thip_window()`
currently requires `Date` columns, not datetimes.

## Filter in the DB, collect explicitly

```{r query, eval=FALSE}
query <- ipd |>
  filter(adm >= as.Date("2023-10-01"), adm < as.Date("2023-10-08")) |>
  thip_filter_icd(codes = "K35", cols = "pdx", match = "prefix")

show_query(query)           # Inspect SQL
candidate_rows <- collect(query)  # Admissions enter R here
```

`thip_filter_icd()` retains matching rows; it does not aggregate people or add
flags. `icd_flag()` operates on local records and returns flags aggregated by
an explicit ID. Neither function supplies validated clinical definitions.

Building a lazy query may read metadata. Printing a lazy dbplyr table can fetch
preview rows; `collect()` is not the only possible trigger for a DB query.
Printing a `thip_window()` plan itself only describes the plan. Use ordinary
`DBI::dbDisconnect(con)` when finished.
